title: Azure Data Factory – Core Concepts & Pipeline Design
summary: Overview of Azure Data Factory pipelines, activities, data flows, linked services, and triggers for data integration.
content:
Azure Data Factory (ADF) is a cloud-based data integration service for creating automated ETL and ELT data pipelines.

Key Components:
- Pipelines: Logical grouping of activities that perform a task.
- Activities: Single processing steps (Copy Activity, Databricks Notebook, Execute Pipeline, Web Activity).
- Datasets: Named structures pointing to data stores (SQL DB, Blob Storage, ADLS Gen2).
- Linked Services: Connection strings defining how ADF connects to external resources.
- Integration Runtimes (IR): Compute infrastructure powering execution (Azure IR, Self-Hosted IR for on-prem).

title: Databricks & PySpark – Data Processing Patterns
summary: Best practices for writing distributed Spark jobs in Python, Delta Lake optimizations, and cluster management.
content:
Azure Databricks provides a managed Apache Spark environment tailored for large-scale data transformation.

Core Techniques:
- Delta Lake: ACID transactions, time travel (`VERSION AS OF`), and schema enforcement.
- Dataframe API: Prefer vectorized PySpark operations over python UDFs for maximum execution speed.
- Partitioning & Z-Ordering: Use `OPTIMIZE table ZORDER BY (col)` to reduce read scan volumes.
- Memory Management: Watch out for shuffle spill and adjust `spark.sql.shuffle.partitions`.

title: Azure Event Hub vs. Service Bus – Event-Driven Architecture
summary: Architectural guidelines for selecting between telemetry event streaming (Event Hub) and high-value transactional messaging (Service Bus).
content:
Selecting the right Azure messaging service:

1. Azure Event Hubs:
- Designed for high-throughput big data streaming (telemetry, log ingestion, IoT).
- Partition-based consumer model with high parallelism.
- Time-series replay capabilities.

2. Azure Service Bus:
- Messaging broker for transactions and workflow decoupling.
- Features: Queues, Topics & Subscriptions, Dead-lettering, Duplicate detection, FIFO sessions.

title: Google Gemini 2.0 Flash API – RAG & Multimodal AI Integration
summary: Implementing low-latency RAG chat, structured output generation, and system instructions with Gemini 2.0 Flash.
content:
Google Gemini 2.0 Flash provides ultra-fast inference with a 1M+ token context window, making it ideal for real-time document Q&A and video transcript analysis.

Implementation Notes:
- Endpoint: `generativelanguage.googleapis.com/v1beta/models/gemini-2.0-flash:generateContent`
- Auth: `key=YOUR_GEMINI_API_KEY` (from Google AI Studio)
- System Instructions: Pass system context in systemInstruction or initial conversation turn to constrain responses.
- Streaming: Use Server-Sent Events (SSE) `streamGenerateContent` for real-time token rendering.

title: Ollama Local LLM – Offline Privacy-First AI Workflow
summary: Configuring local qwen2.5:7b model for private document chat, zero API cost, and local REST API access.
content:
Ollama allows running open-source LLMs locally on `localhost:11434` without internet access or API fees.

Setup:
- Model: `ollama run qwen2.5:7b` (32k context window, excellent Czech language support).
- Endpoint: `POST http://localhost:11434/api/generate` or `/api/chat`.
- CORS: Set `OLLAMA_ORIGINS="*"` if calling directly from browser frontend.
- Integration: Serve as private fallback when offline or for sensitive local memory queries.

title: P.A.R.A. System – Personal Information Architecture
summary: Tiago Forte's P.A.R.A. framework for organizing digital life into Projects, Areas, Resources, and Archives.
content:
The P.A.R.A. method categorizes every piece of information into 4 distinct pillars:

1. 10 PROJECTS: Active efforts with specific goals and deadlines (e.g. AIVOS Build, Cloud Certifications).
2. 20 AREAS: Ongoing responsibilities to maintain over time (e.g. Career, Health, AI Learning).
3. 30 RESOURCES: Topics of interest and reference materials (e.g. ADF Docs, PySpark Snippets).
4. 40 ARCHIVES: Inactive items from the other 3 categories held for reference.

title: Python Data Pipelines – BeautifulSoup, Pandas & yt-dlp
summary: Automating data extraction from web pages, YouTube playlists, and tabular data transformation.
content:
Building Python automation scripts for data collection:

- Web Extraction: Use `BeautifulSoup` + `requests` for static HTML parsing or `playwright` for JS rendering.
- YouTube Audio/Subtitles: Use `yt-dlp --write-auto-sub --skip-download` to fetch video transcripts efficiently without downloading large video files.
- Structured Output: Process raw payloads with `pandas` and export clean JSON / CSV datasets.

title: Power BI & DAX – Data Modeling
summary: Star schema design, DAX time intelligence functions, and What-If parameter modeling.
content:
Key principles for scalable Power BI report design:

- Star Schema: Separate Fact tables (sales, events) from Dimension tables (date, customer, product).
- DAX Measures: Keep measures decoupled from columns; use `CALCULATE`, `SAMEPERIODLASTYEAR`, `DATESYTD` for time intelligence.
- Performance: Avoid bi-directional relationships on large tables; use `USERELATIONSHIP` explicitly when needed.
